description:
Scope: coverage-only planning for lib/zaq/channels/identity_scope.ex:28. No production implementation, new operation, agent tool, docs change, DB migration, or E2E journey. Exclusive test path for this issue: test/zaq/channels/identity_scope_test.exs (NEW). Do not edit other test paths; existing People tests are context, not a second owner.

Functional contract and infrastructure audit: Zaq.Channels.IdentityScope.authority/2 owns native identity authority; existing Zaq.Accounts.PersonIdentities.key/2 calls it and its DB-backed identity resolver tests live at test/zaq/people/identity_resolver_test.exs. Channels policy docs/services/channels.md:21-34 requires Mattermost native IDs to be scoped to canonical server endpoint including deployment path; unknown/unattested tenant scope stays connector-local. Current module has no focused tests. Reuse its real public authority/2; add no Actions, mocks, fake clients or seams. Action reuse assessment: not applicable: tests only, no executable operation changed, no new consumers/permissions/side effects; existing IdentityScope.authority/2 is the operation being verified. No docs update necessary unless actual behavior differs from documented contract (then flag discrepancy, do not silently alter it).

Tests to add before any implementation (all in exclusive file above; use ExUnit.Case, async: true, alias Zaq.Channels.IdentityScope):
1. Regression directly covering missed line 28: authority("mattermost", %{id: 41, url: "ftp://chat.example.test/team"}) == "connector:41". URI.parse yields host but disallowed scheme; it must enter the inner case fallback, not the generic function clause or the valid URI branch. Assert independently expected exact key (never URL/global). With %{id: 42} same malformed URL yields "connector:42" to prove connector isolation; do not derive expected result using production implementation.
2. Other side of the inner guard: hostless http(s) URI (e.g. "https:///team", confirm URI.parse shape if parser-version behavior differs, choose a hostless parseable URI) with id 41 also returns "connector:41". This establishes fallback for missing host, distinct from disallowed scheme. Verify exact key, not only non-nil.
3. Invalid Mattermost endpoint without an attested integer connector ID (%{url: "ftp://chat.example.test/team"}, and if useful id: nil) returns "unscoped". Line 28 then connector_authority/1 generic fallback must not become a global or a guessed server scope. For config id 0/negative, avoid asserting rejection: current guard is is_integer/1, not positive-integer validation; any desired stricter contract is separate production work.
4. Contrast with valid canonical endpoint: authority("mattermost", %{id: 41, url: "HTTPS://CHAT.EXAMPLE.TEST/team/"}) should only be used if URI.parse actually recognizes uppercase scheme; otherwise use lowercase scheme with uppercase host. Assert "https://chat.example.test/team" for URL "https://CHAT.EXAMPLE.TEST/team/"; optionally include userinfo/query/fragment, asserting they are removed while deployment path remains. This protects the good branch against tests accidentally passing via generic fallback.
5. Adjacent branch sanity as needed: missing/nonbinary url falls through generic authority/2 to connector-scoped key; email/telegram/discord return "global" regardless of invalid config, and another unsupported platform stays connector-local. These are distinct clauses, not prerequisites for covering line 28; keep few focused examples rather than a Cartesian suite.

Property assessment: authority is a permission-sensitive scope default, so add a small focused ExUnitProperties/StreamData property in the same file: for bounded positive integer ids (1..10000) and member_of(["ftp", "ws", "file"]) construct scheme://chat.example.test/team; each non-http(s) URL resolves to exactly "connector:#{id}", never global or a shared server authority. Use a second generated distinct id only if useful to explicitly prove isolation; do not generate arbitrary garbage or recreate URI normalization in the assertion. Concrete example #1 remains mandatory. If these scheme inputs unexpectedly produce a valid http(s) URI on a dependency version, use a constrained known-disallowed URI set and document it rather than weakening the security assertion.

Fixtures/helpers: literal map configs with only :id/:url, deterministic fixed host/path; no factories, Repo, process, persistent state, clocks, sleeps, or helper abstraction needed. Existing channels tests use async ExUnit.Case. Mocking plan: none; URI and IdentityScope run for real, with no external API. Isolation: async: true, no global application environment or SQL Sandbox; no special synchronization. Observable assertions: exact authority strings and connector separation; no private-function or implementation-call assertions.

Unreachable/blocked paths: line 28 is reachable via public authority/2 with %{url: binary}; no known blocker. Missing/nonbinary url never reaches that line by design; testing it exercises the outer fallback, not line 28. Invalid platform does likewise. If a hostless candidate does not take the expected URI.parse path, replace it with a known hostless binary and note the limitation; do not introduce a test hook. If execution demonstrates current production behavior contradicts the documented policy, report a separate behavioral issue rather than changing production in this coverage-only task.

Validation handoff (for implementer, not run in planning): first write focused examples/property, run mix test test/zaq/channels/identity_scope_test.exs (isolated, through Context Mode) and ensure line 28 is hit in a fresh successful coverage report as part of the coverage-upper workflow. Review branch behavior and file-local coverage, not merely total ratio. Then run mix q plus isolated tests per docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md phase 4; final mix precommit only at final human approval gate per phase 6. On failure/timeouts diagnose and rerun fresh, never use stale coverage. No E2E needed: pure transport-authority calculation, no UI journey. Preserve existing assertions. No application tests executed during planning.
title: [coverage] Cover IdentityScope invalid Mattermost endpoint fallback (line 28)
